evidence: The original edit replaced `[LAW:*]` with bare `LAW:`, which is inconsistent with the bracketed `[INV:visible-skeleton]` form on line 49, so the reviewer's inconsistency was real. Its suggested `[LAW:token]` would have failed the gate the PR existed to fix, since the agent says the scanner is a bare regex over `git ls-files` with no code-span exemption. The agent kept the diagnosis and used the bracketed canonical `[LAW:no-silent-failure]`, which round 1 shows as the change.
guidance_note: When a scanner rejects a placeholder token in prose, replace it with a real canonical example in the same bracketed form instead of stripping the syntax, so the fix stays consistent with the doc's other examples.

narrative: A one-line docs fix to unbreak the law-token gate replaced the bracketed placeholder with a bare `LAW:`. The reviewer correctly flagged the format inconsistency but suggested a placeholder that would re-break the gate. The agent took the diagnosis, wrote a different fix with a canonical bracketed token, verified it with `go test ./internal/lawtokens/`, and round 1 approved. It first quoted a wrong SHA and corrected it in a follow-up reply.
guidance_observations: The agent quoted a fix SHA before reading it back and had to post a correction; read the pushed SHA from git before replying.
The agent's pushback named the exact mechanism (scanner regex, no fence exemption, `lawtokens.Canonical`), which made the rejection of the suggested cure checkable.

evidence: The hunk shows `acyclic bool // engine enforces for Dependency always`, and both examples write `acyclic: true` on dependency relations. The doc never says what `acyclic: false` on a Dependency does, so the type admits an undefined combination. The thread was resolved with no reply, and the PR merged on its single commit, so the doc never changed.
guidance_note: When a field is always forced on for one variant, model it so the variant cannot carry it (for example, acyclic only on Reference) before writing examples that set it.

evidence: FieldDef declares `merge MergeStrategy`, and every example field in the hunks has only kind/required/values with no `merge:` key. Nothing visible in the packet states a default. The thread was resolved silently and the doc merged unchanged.
guidance_note: Before publishing a meta-model with worked examples, walk every FieldDef facet against every example field and either set it or state the default for omission.

evidence: The hunk itself reads "Today's five leaf types (`task|feature|bug|chore`)", which lists four, so the count error shows in the line. The PR had one commit and merged after the thread was resolved with no reply, so the wrong count shipped.
guidance_note: Recount any enumerated list against the number stated in the same sentence before committing prose.

evidence: The reviewer says ../event-store/design.md has no §config-stream or §validation heading, and names the real sections. That document is not in the packet, so the claim cannot be checked here. If the claim is true, the silent resolve left broken anchors in the merged doc.
guidance_note: When citing sections of a sibling design doc, copy the anchor from that doc's actual headings rather than naming the concept.

evidence: The meta-model declares `between [](TypeName, TypeName)` with TypeName a key of `types`, and the example writes `between: [[any, any]]`, but no `any` type is declared in either visible types map. Nothing in the shown hunks introduces `any` as a reserved wildcard. The thread was resolved with no reply.
guidance_note: When an example uses a value outside the declared grammar (a wildcard), add it to the meta-model as a named reserved term in the same edit.

evidence: The hunk cites `../event-store/design.md §derived-state`. The reviewer says that heading does not exist and the content is under §fold, but the event-store doc is not in the packet. This is the same anchor-accuracy question as F4 at another site, raised in the same round.
guidance_note: When one cross-doc anchor is wrong, check every other §anchor citing the same doc in that pass.

evidence: The hunk states "every field declares `exposure` at birth", yet no example field sets `exposure:`. The custom profile guards `review` on `requires: [{present: description}]`, so the rule that guard fields must be structural is left unresolved for `description`. The thread was resolved silently.
guidance_note: When the prose states a rule that every field must declare X, make the worked examples declare X, especially on fields that the rule constrains (guard inputs).

evidence: The grammar shows `children` and `lifecycle Rollup{} | Machine{...}` as independent fields, so rollup on a leaf is representable, which is a real gap. The claim that a container's Machine would "double-count" children's stages is speculation the doc does not support. The real part still deserved an invariant or an OPEN note, and got no reply.
guidance_note: For each sum-typed field in a meta-model, write down which combinations with sibling fields are illegal, and either encode them in the type or list them among the structural-layer invariants.

evidence: The hunk shows `depends` between `[[feature, feature], [story, story]]` and `story` marked `work-unit: true`. The `feature` definition and the Scheduling section the reviewer quotes are not in the packet, so whether feature-level edges are undefined under `next` cannot be confirmed. The thread was resolved with no reply.
guidance_note: When an example declares dependency edges between a type, check that the scheduling section says how edges on that type, whether work-unit or not, feed `next`.

narrative: A 437-line draft design doc got nine findings in one round. Several are verifiable from the hunks alone: the five-vs-four leaf-type count, `any` outside the declared grammar, and examples omitting the exposure and merge facets the prose says are mandatory. Every thread was resolved by the author with no reply, and the PR merged on its original single commit, so none were addressed or rebutted on the record. No finding was fix-caused because no fix commit exists.
guidance_observations: Resolving all nine threads silently and merging the unchanged commit skipped address-pr-reviews entirely, and at least one plain factual error ("five leaf types" listing four) shipped as a result.

If a draft doc is deliberately merged with known gaps, a one-line reply per thread (deferred to §open or rejected with reason) keeps the review record honest. A bare resolve leaves no trace of whether a finding was judged at all.
